structure: 100 composers × 3 patterns × 10 s over a continuous stream
architecture: <audio> + createMediaElementSource + 4 s ring buffer + two crossfade buses with per-slot bed

patterns.title: Train gains momentum
patterns.principle: Motif microloups accelerate from 0.4 to 0.05 s — ostinato as mechanical acceleration.
patterns.reference: «Le chemin de fer» op. 27 (1844) — the first depiction of a railway in music.

patterns.title: Aesop's feast: 8 variations
patterns.principle: A short motif repeats alternating forward and backward — variational obsession.
patterns.reference: «Le festin d'Ésope» op. 39 (1839): 25 variations on a single theme.

patterns.title: Symphony for solo piano
patterns.principle: Octave layers and dense saturation — one instrument pretends to be an orchestra.
patterns.reference: «Symphonie» from the 12 Études op. 39 (1857): piano as orchestra.

patterns.title: Mechanical ballet
patterns.principle: 16 synchronized metronome clicks over a low humming propeller drone.
patterns.reference: «Ballet mécanique» (1924/25): mechanical pianos, airplane propellers, electric bells.

patterns.title: Airplane propellers
patterns.principle: Deep amplitude modulation at 22 Hz turns the material into propeller rumble.
patterns.reference: The «Ballet mécanique» score prescribes actual aircraft propellers.

patterns.title: Electric bells
patterns.principle: Inharmonic resonator bank: metallic strikes, sparse rhythmic mask.
patterns.reference: Bells and sirens were part of the original 1925 instrumentation.

patterns.title: Urban Sax: the city as stage
patterns.principle: Eight scattered diffusion points — sound dispersed across an imagined city.
patterns.reference: Urban Sax (1973): dozens of saxophonists on rooftops, squares, and parks.

patterns.title: Swarm of saxophones
patterns.principle: Twelve detuned copies form a breathing mass of one timbre.
patterns.reference: Artman's mass saxophone ensembles are minimalist drone compositions.

patterns.title: Lard Free: motorik
patterns.principle: Continuous 4/4 krautrock pulse with tape echo.
patterns.reference: Lard Free — Artman's krautrock band of the mid-1970s.

patterns.title: Spectral growth
patterns.principle: Resonators on the stream's own peaks gradually build up — sound grows itself.
patterns.reference: Romanian spectral school: Avram and Dumitrescu, spectralism outside schools.

patterns.title: Arborescences
patterns.principle: Branching overtones 1 : 1.5 : 2.25 : 3.375 enter one by one.
patterns.reference: Her orchestral branches grow from one sound like a living structure.

patterns.title: Inner light
patterns.principle: Granular freeze slowly brightens through a filter — contemplation of a single moment.
patterns.reference: Spectral meditation: duration as a way of listening.

patterns.title: Folk line
patterns.principle: Fifth-octave doubling with light vibrato — a folk melody inside the avant-garde.
patterns.reference: Balada: synthesis of Spanish folklore and hard-edged avant-garde, Carnegie Mellon.

patterns.title: Cluster background
patterns.principle: 13 semitone copies — a dense cluster beneath the melody.
patterns.reference: His cluster writing of the 1960–70s: folklore against sound masses.

patterns.title: Sinfonía negra
patterns.principle: Dark ostinato gate and low resonances — ritual drama.
patterns.reference: «Sinfonía negra» (1968) — Afro-Cuban roots in symphonic fabric.

patterns.title: File inside a silo
patterns.principle: Long metallic combs and echo — the acoustics of an industrial tank.
patterns.reference: Bandt voices silos, tanks, and industrial chambers of Australia.

patterns.title: Flagong: glass
patterns.principle: Glass inharmonic resonances 1 : 2.32 : 4.25 : 6.63 — a fragile shimmering fabric.
patterns.reference: Flagong (1978) — her playable glass sound sculpture.

patterns.title: Sound landscape
patterns.principle: Slow spatial diffusion, source almost dry — place matters more than processing.
patterns.reference: Pioneer of Australian sound art and acoustic ecology, books on sound sculpture.

patterns.title: Brassage
patterns.principle: Granular tape mixing: random 30 ms grains — a GRM classic.
patterns.reference: Bayle headed GRM; brassage is the signature technique of the Groupe de Recherches Musicales.

patterns.title: Time freeze
patterns.principle: A single instant stuck in a granular loop with micro-jitter.
patterns.reference: «L'Expérience acoustique» (1969–72): a journey inside sound.

patterns.title: Acousmatic montage
patterns.principle: Random splice of fragments: the cause of the sound vanishes, only the gesture remains.
patterns.reference: Acousmatics: sound without visible source, montage as dramaturgy.

patterns.title: Intervallic cells
patterns.principle: Minor seventh and minor ninth as harmonic cells — clarity instead of mass.
patterns.reference: «Ideas of Order» (1952): neoclassicism shading into serialism.

patterns.title: Neoclassical clarity
patterns.principle: Clean bandpass filter and accented gate — chamber discipline.
patterns.reference: A Stravinskian line: transparent texture, sharp accents.

patterns.title: Serialization of order
patterns.principle: Deterministic permutation of fragments — order as a compositional gesture.
patterns.reference: Late Berger: serial organization while retaining clarity.

patterns.title: Thema: homage to the project
patterns.principle: Scanning granulation and filter sweep — the stream turns into abstraction.
patterns.reference: «Thema (Omaggio a Joyce)» (1958): Cathy Berberian reads Joyce, tape transforms the voice. Ancestor of this project.

patterns.title: Sequenza: virtuoso voice
patterns.principle: Explosive micro-stutters and dynamic waves — extreme vocal gesturality.
patterns.reference: «Sequenza III» (1965): the voice as theater of all possible states.

patterns.title: Sinfonia: palimpsest
patterns.principle: Cloud of copies and collage of quotes — layers of music on top of music.
patterns.reference: «Sinfonia» (1968): Mahler's scherzo as a river carrying the debris of history.

patterns.title: Music of the Spheres
patterns.principle: Sliding sine layers — electric glissandi of the 1930s.
patterns.reference: «Music of the Spheres» (1938) — an early electronic score, forgotten for decades.

patterns.title: Clusters
patterns.principle: Semitone cluster ±6 semitones — piano masses.
patterns.reference: «Clusters» (1936): clusters performed through hand choreography.

patterns.title: Cluster choreography
patterns.principle: Cluster turns on and off with a rhythmic gate — hand motion as rhythm.
patterns.reference: Beyer choreographed cluster performance — the body as score.

patterns.title: Vespertine: microbeats
patterns.principle: 20 ms grains, 40 per second — intimate micro-percussion from the stream itself.
patterns.reference: «Vespertine» (2001): Matmos built beats from footsteps, cards, whispers.

patterns.title: Medúlla: voice only
patterns.principle: Formant choir and octave layers — everything made from vocal matter.
patterns.reference: «Medúlla» (2004) — an album assembled entirely from voices.

patterns.title: Biophilia: gravity harp
patterns.principle: Pendulum pitch relations and a slow drone — music of natural forces.
patterns.reference: «Biophilia» (2011): pendulum harp, sonification of gravity.

patterns.title: Répons
patterns.principle: Spatial rotation, resonator chord, echo — soloist and electronic aura.
patterns.reference: «Répons» (1981–84), IRCAM: live soloists and computer spatialization.

patterns.title: Anthèmes 2
patterns.principle: Harmonizer and fast panoramic gestures follow the sound.
patterns.reference: «Anthèmes 2» (1997): violin and live-electronics, score-following.

patterns.title: IRCAM machine (Boulez #4)
patterns.principle: Granulation, ring modulation, and space in one breath — the engine itself as a fourth Boulez.
patterns.reference: Boulez holds four slots in the list — the fourth, IRCAM, is this machine.

patterns.title: Antiphony: space required
patterns.principle: Left and right channels processed independently and never synchronized.
patterns.reference: «Antiphony 1» (1953): spatial separation is a condition of the music, not an effect.

patterns.title: Ice Field
patterns.principle: Four unsynchronized cloud groups and sparse clicks — a sound landscape of ensembles.
patterns.reference: «Ice Field» (2001), Pulitzer: orchestral groups scattered through the hall.

patterns.title: Unsynchronized ensembles
patterns.principle: Three voices in tempos 1 : 1.07 : 0.93, spread across the field.
patterns.reference: Brant: space is the fourth dimension of music.

patterns.title: For Alto
patterns.principle: Saxophone formant and breathing grains — solo without accompaniment.
patterns.reference: «For Alto» (1968) — the first solo-sax album in jazz history.

patterns.title: Ghost Trance
patterns.principle: Irregular gate and echo — a pulse that is almost a dance.
patterns.reference: Ghost Trance Music (1995–2006): a ritual pulse under improvisation.

patterns.title: Graphic scores
patterns.principle: Fragment collage and pulse markers — diagrams as music.
patterns.reference: His compositions have diagram names: «Composition No. 96» with projectors.

patterns.title: Zikr: repetition as path
patterns.principle: A loop grows in number of repetitions — a Sufi remembrance from the fabric of the stream.
patterns.reference: Sarmad Brody — an Inayati Sufi teacher in Texas, composer, friend of Xenakis.

patterns.title: Echo of Xenakis
patterns.principle: Stochastic grains and a cloud — probabilistic masses in the spirit of his liner notes.
patterns.reference: Brody wrote the liner notes for a Xenakis record on Nonesuch.

patterns.title: In memory of a friend
patterns.principle: A sparse 660 Hz bell and long echo — a hidden motif connected to block 054 Kamin.
patterns.reference: Brody and Kamin died in the same car crash on April 11, 2010.

patterns.title: December 1952
patterns.principle: A random field of sparse events — a graphic score as a field of possibilities.
patterns.reference: «December 1952» — one of the first graphic scores: lines and rectangles.

patterns.title: Available Forms
patterns.principle: Cue splices: the conductor chooses the order — here the seed makes the choice.
patterns.reference: «Available Forms» (1961): forms are available, order is chosen in the moment.

patterns.title: 25 Pages
patterns.principle: Forward and backward alternate randomly — pages played in any order.
patterns.reference: «25 Pages» (1953): 25 pages in any sequence and direction.

patterns.title: Williams Mix
patterns.principle: 200 fragments spliced by lot: aleatoric tape montage.
patterns.reference: «Williams Mix» (1952): 600 fragments cut according to the I Ching.

patterns.title: Prepared piano
patterns.principle: Inharmonic resonators 1 : 1.41 : 2.1 : 3.7 — bolts and screws between the strings.
patterns.reference: Prepared piano (from 1940): a percussion orchestra inside the piano.

patterns.title: 4′33″: near silence
patterns.principle: The stream is muted down to the noise floor — silence in which you hear the room.
patterns.reference: «4′33″» (1952): not silence, but everything that sounds around. Schulhoff preceded him by 33 years.

patterns.title: Trout Mask Replica
patterns.principle: Chaotic splice rehearsed to precision: a 7/8 gate over the collage.
patterns.reference: «Trout Mask Replica» (1969): eight months of rehearsal for the sake of chaos.

patterns.title: Polyrhythm 3 against 4
patterns.principle: Gate 3+3+2 against 4/4 clicks — two pulses do not meet.
patterns.reference: Magic Band: polyrhythmic density of blues played as chamber avant-garde.

patterns.title: Dachau Blues
patterns.principle: Fuzz saturation and a wailing formant — voice at its limit.
patterns.reference: His vocal range was four and a half octaves, from growl to falsetto.

patterns.title: Metric modulation 4:5
patterns.principle: The delay grows as a tempo shift 1→1.25 — time flows smoothly.
patterns.reference: Cello Sonata (1948): tempo change through a shared duration — Carter's signature device.

patterns.title: Strata
patterns.principle: Three tempo layers 1 : 1.25 : 0.8 — independent musical characters.
patterns.reference: String Quartet No. 1 (1951): layer-characters in their own tempos.

patterns.title: Night Fantasies
patterns.principle: A slow cloud and dynamic waves — nocturnal fluidity.
patterns.reference: «Night Fantasies» (1980): piano fabric that never repeats.

patterns.title: Sinfonía india
patterns.principle: Driving ostinato and wooden clicks — indigenous percussion in the orchestra.
patterns.reference: «Sinfonía india» (1935): themes of Mexican Indians, huéhuetl and teponaztli.

patterns.title: Teponaztli
patterns.principle: Wooden resonances 1 : 3.1 : 5.2 — a slit drum.
patterns.reference: The Aztec teponaztli is a wooden slit drum with two tongues.

patterns.title: Open harmonies
patterns.principle: Fifths and major thirds — a transparent, republican clarity.
patterns.reference: His harmonic language: open intervals, archaism, and modernism.

patterns.title: Harmolodics
patterns.principle: Three transposed copies of one line drift independently — no principal key.
patterns.reference: Harmolodics: all voices equal, the melody lives in all tunings at once.

patterns.title: Free Jazz
patterns.principle: Jittered grains and a swing gate — collective improvisation of a double quartet.
patterns.reference: «Free Jazz» (1960): two quartets improvise simultaneously for 38 minutes.

patterns.title: Dancing in Your Head
patterns.principle: A loop-chant and a calling oscillator — jazz as ritual.
patterns.reference: «Dancing in Your Head» (1977): recorded with the Master Musicians of Jajouka.

patterns.title: Tone clusters
patterns.principle: 13 semitone copies — a cluster played with palm and forearm.
patterns.reference: «The Tides of Manaunaun» (1917): clusters as part of the musical language.

patterns.title: String piano
patterns.principle: Freeze with jitter and high resonances — plucks and glissandi on the strings.
patterns.reference: «Aeolian Harp» (1923): playing directly on the piano strings.

patterns.title: New Musical Resources
patterns.principle: Tempo canon 1 : 4/3 : 5/3 — rhythm from harmonic ratios.
patterns.reference: The book «New Musical Resources» (1930): rhythmic ratios equal harmonic ones.

patterns.title: Black Angels
patterns.principle: Electric saturation, metallic resonances, tremolo — an amplified string quartet.
patterns.reference: «Black Angels» (1970): electric string quartet, gongs, crystals, shouts.

patterns.title: Vox Balaenae
patterns.principle: Whale-call glissando and a formant mask — performers in masks.
patterns.reference: «Vox Balaenae» (1971): electric flute, cello, piano; masks.

patterns.title: Numerology 7 and 13
patterns.principle: Rhythmic mask 7+13 — his numerical magic.
patterns.reference: Crumb built forms on the numbers 7 and 13 — «Vox Balaenae», «Makrokosmos».

patterns.title: Hypercollage
patterns.principle: 300 splices and a granular layer — extreme montage density.
patterns.reference: Curran: hyper-energetic tape collages, Musica Elettronica Viva.

patterns.title: A Rose Is a Round
patterns.principle: Three identical voices with staggered entries — a circle canon.
patterns.reference: «A Rose Is a Rose Is a Round» — a vocal circle as collage.

patterns.title: Schtyx
patterns.principle: Folk-jitter gate and intervallic layers — roots in the avant-garde.
patterns.reference: «Schtyx» (1988): Jewish melodic roots in new fabric.

patterns.title: Synchronisms: instrument and tape
patterns.principle: Dry voice and granular shadow synchronize on attacks.
patterns.reference: The «Synchronisms» cycle (from 1962): live instrument and tape as one hybrid.

patterns.title: Synchronization point
patterns.principle: Micro-stutters on attacks and a ping oscillator — tape answers the instrument.
patterns.reference: «Synchronisms No. 6» (1970), Pulitzer: piano and tape.

patterns.title: Divergence
patterns.principle: Two copies begin in sync and drift apart in phase.
patterns.reference: The dramaturgy of the cycle: union of live and electronic, their fusion and rupture.

patterns.title: Eight Songs for a Mad King
patterns.principle: Extreme formants and stutters — voice on the edge of madness.
patterns.reference: «Eight Songs for a Mad King» (1969): King George III sings across four octaves.

patterns.title: Foxtrot inside the symphony
patterns.principle: A buried dance gate is deformed by a filter.
patterns.reference: «St. Thomas Wake» (1969): a foxtrot distorted into a symphonic shadow.

patterns.title: Farewell to Stromness
patterns.principle: Nearly dry sound and soft harmonization — farewell simplicity.
patterns.reference: «Farewell to Stromness» (1980) — his most famous, tender piece.

patterns.title: ACEZANTEZ
patterns.principle: Theatrical collage and click-gestures — a stage without words.
patterns.reference: ACEZANTEZ (Zagreb, 1971): Detoni's musical theater ensemble.

patterns.title: Phonomorphia
patterns.principle: Granular morph through the material — sound metamorphoses.
patterns.reference: His phonomorphias — a theater of sonic metamorphoses.

patterns.title: Stage without words
patterns.principle: Formant characters and rhythmic gestures.
patterns.reference: Detoni: composer, pianist and writer, musical theater as method.

patterns.title: Gris-Gris
patterns.principle: Second-line gate and swamp echo — New Orleans voodoo psychedelia.
patterns.reference: «Gris-Gris» (1968): voodoo ritual as psychedelic album.

patterns.title: Voodoo chant
patterns.principle: Fifth doubling and tremolo — incantation in layers.
patterns.reference: His chants trace back to New Orleans rituals and Mardi Gras Indians.

patterns.title: Night Tripper
patterns.principle: Slow panorama and saturation — a night tripper in space.
patterns.reference: The Night Tripper stage persona: feathers, skulls, swamp groove.

patterns.title: Any Resemblance…
patterns.principle: A recognizable motif stays dry, alien synthesis around it.
patterns.reference: «Any Resemblance Is Purely Coincidental» (1980): Caruso sings inside computer music.

patterns.title: The Earth Is My Mother
patterns.principle: Formant singer and harmonic layers — a synthesized voice.
patterns.reference: «The Earth Is My Mother» — the computer voice as a solo instrument.

patterns.title: Bell Labs
patterns.principle: Ring modulation and early computer grains — 1960s aesthetics.
patterns.reference: Dodge worked at Bell Labs — the cradle of computer music.

patterns.title: Animus: duel
patterns.principle: Aggressive tape-antagonist against a dry protagonist.
patterns.reference: «Animus I» (1966): trombone and tape as opponents in a drama.

patterns.title: Prism: quotes
patterns.principle: Collage of debris and a cloud — refraction of other people's music.
patterns.reference: «Prism» (1969): quotes from Berio, Bach, Mahler in an orchestral prism.

patterns.title: Windows
patterns.principle: Spatial orchestral waves — windows into a sound field.
patterns.reference: «Windows» (1972), Pulitzer: orchestral windows of memory.

patterns.title: Inside sound
patterns.principle: Freeze and resonators on peaks — microscopic listening.
patterns.reference: Romanian spectralism: Dumitrescu and Avram, music inside sound.

patterns.title: Glissando textures
patterns.principle: A slowly diverging cloud — his long mass glissandi.
patterns.reference: His orchestral textures glide continuously like living matter.

patterns.title: Aphonic: spectral silence
patterns.principle: Near silence and rare grains — sound on the threshold of hearing.
patterns.reference: Spectral asceticism: extreme concentration on the small.

patterns.title: Water Concerto
patterns.principle: Water filter sweeps and drop-grains — water as instrument.
patterns.reference: «Water Concerto» (1998): water percussion in a basin, orchestra responds.

patterns.title: Organic Music: paper
patterns.principle: Noise resonances and transients — paper and wood as instruments.
patterns.reference: His organic music: paper, water, stones, ceramics.

patterns.title: Ritual
patterns.principle: Slow gate and a bell — shamanic theater.
patterns.reference: Opera «Marco Polo» (1996): ritual as musical form.

patterns.title: Interspecies dialogue
patterns.principle: Transposition ×4 and echo-answer — a conversation with the non-human.
patterns.reference: Dunn: bioacoustics, attempts at dialogue with birds and insects.

patterns.title: Avian range
patterns.principle: Transposition ×6 and chirp-grains — the stream in the avian register.
patterns.reference: His works explore how animals hear the world.

patterns.title: Insects
patterns.principle: 40 Hz tremolo and high resonances — stridulation.
patterns.reference: Dunn recorded bark beetles and built interspecies interfaces.

patterns.title: Jungle growl
patterns.principle: 24 Hz tremolo and a bandpass wah — the growling brass of the Cotton Club.
patterns.reference: Jungle style (1920s): growl trumpets of Bubber Miley and Tricky Sam Nanton.

patterns.title: Ellington effect
patterns.principle: Mixing formant resonances — timbre as collective creation.
patterns.reference: Ellington effect: he wrote not for instruments but for specific people of the orchestra.

patterns.title: Take the A Train
patterns.principle: Swing gate and harmonization — the orchestra's signature tune.
patterns.reference: «Take the 'A' Train» (1941, Strayhorn) — the theme of the Ellington orchestra.

patterns.title: Trombone + tape
patterns.principle: Sliding formant and ring modulation — brass and electronics.
patterns.reference: Erb: trombonist and composer, pioneer of live-electronics for brass.

patterns.title: The Seventh Trumpet
patterns.principle: Brass resonances and echo — a theatrical trumpet.
patterns.reference: «The Seventh Trumpet» (1969) — his brass-electronic theater.

patterns.title: Brass theater
patterns.principle: Panoramic gestures and saturation — the instrument as character.
patterns.reference: His brass concertos with tape — the drama of soloist and electronics.

patterns.title: Silence and duration
patterns.principle: −18 dB, long resonances — sound allowed to be itself.
patterns.reference: «Triadic Memories» (1981): 90 minutes of quiet, almost static music.

patterns.title: Rare events
patterns.principle: Gate passes only a few attacks of the stream, long echo between them.
patterns.reference: Late Feldman: events as rare as stars in emptiness.

patterns.title: Let it be
patterns.principle: Nearly dry sound, dark spectral tilt — non-intervention as method.
patterns.reference: Let sound be itself — his aesthetic of non-intervention.

patterns.title: Baroque Variations: erasure
patterns.principle: Progressive subtraction of the stream's own peaks — down to a ghost.
patterns.reference: «Baroque Variations» (1967): Bach, Handel, Scarlatti erased to semi-transparency.

patterns.title: Phorion
patterns.principle: Ghost collage: debris of the recognizable in alien fabric.
patterns.reference: «Phorion» — part of «Baroque Variations», Bach as mirage.

patterns.title: Improvisation ensemble
patterns.principle: Free cloud and gate — collective improvisation of 1957.
patterns.reference: Foss founded the Improvisation Chamber Ensemble (1957) — rare for an academic.

patterns.title: Linguistics of sound
patterns.principle: Phoneme-grains of 30 ms and formants — speech as musical matter.
patterns.reference: Gaburo: musical language, compositional linguistics.

patterns.title: Lemon Drops
patterns.principle: Bell-drops and echo — early electronics.
patterns.reference: «Lemon Drops» (1965) — his electronic miniature.

patterns.title: Antiphony III
patterns.principle: Voice and tape in space — antiphony of live and electronic.
patterns.reference: «Antiphony III (Pearl-white moments)» (1962): voice and tape.

patterns.title: Rhapsody: glissando
patterns.principle: Ascending glissando oscillator and harmonization — the famous clarinet climb.
patterns.reference: «Rhapsody in Blue» (1924): clarinet glissando, improvised at rehearsal.

patterns.title: Blue notes
patterns.principle: Minor third and minor seventh against major — blues coloring.
patterns.reference: His language: blues notes inside European harmony.

patterns.title: Swing
patterns.principle: Swing gate over almost-dry sound.
patterns.reference: Gershwin joined jazz rhythm to concert form.

patterns.title: City of Glass
patterns.principle: Dissonant cloud and brass saturation — a city of glass and brass.
patterns.reference: «City of Glass» (1951) for the Stan Kenton orchestra: an atonal jazz monument.

patterns.title: Atonal brass
patterns.principle: Brass resonances and percussive stabs.
patterns.reference: Graettinger: radical atonalism inside a big band.

patterns.title: This Modern World
patterns.principle: Tempo strata — anxious density.
patterns.reference: «This Modern World» (1953) — his second suite for Kenton.

patterns.title: Quarter tones
patterns.principle: Harmonization in quarter-tone ratios 2^(1/24), 2^(3/24), 2^(5/24).
patterns.reference: Hába: quarter-tone system, Prague 1920s, special instruments.

patterns.title: 24-EDO grid
patterns.principle: Resonators on a quarter-tone grid — a new harmonic landscape.
patterns.reference: His theory: 24 steps per octave, sixth-tone harmony.

patterns.title: Matka
patterns.principle: Grains and a quarter-tone layer — an opera in microtones.
patterns.reference: Quarter-tone opera «Matka» (1931).

patterns.title: Gamelan
patterns.principle: Metallic resonances in an approximation of slendro — a gamelan from the stream.
patterns.reference: Harrison built an American gamelan with William Colvig.

patterns.title: Just intonation
patterns.principle: Harmonization in just ratios 9/8, 5/4, 3/2, 5/3.
patterns.reference: Just intonation — his harmonic faith.

patterns.title: Prepared piano
patterns.principle: Inharmonic resonators — legacy of working with Cage.
patterns.reference: Harrison and Cage: prepared piano, 1940s.

patterns.title: 44 tropes
patterns.principle: Deterministic permutation of 44 fragments — his trope system.
patterns.reference: Hauer: 44 tropes of 12 tones, a system earlier than Schoenberg (1919).

patterns.title: 12-tone grid
patterns.principle: Resonators on an equal 12-tone grid.
patterns.reference: His Zwölftonmusik: law and play.

patterns.title: Zwölftonspiel
patterns.principle: Gate and row harmonization — playing by the law.
patterns.reference: Zwölftonspiele — his meditative 12-tone games.

patterns.title: Fuzz + feedback
patterns.principle: Asymmetric fuzz and self-exciting resonant peak.
patterns.reference: Fuzz Face and controlled feedback — his voice (1967–70).

patterns.title: Univibe
patterns.principle: Slow tremolo and panorama — four-stage phase vortex.
patterns.reference: Uni-Vibe (1968): «Machine Gun», Woodstock.

patterns.title: Backwards guitar
patterns.principle: Reverse tape and echo — a flipped solo.
patterns.reference: «Are You Experienced?» (1967): backward guitar solos.

patterns.title: Voile d'Orphée
patterns.principle: Tearing grains and a filter sweep — Orpheus's veil tears.
patterns.reference: «Le Voile d'Orphée» (1953): Henry's first concrete drama.

patterns.title: Porte et soupir
patterns.principle: Creak-stutters and breathing pauses — the door and the sigh.
patterns.reference: «Variations pour une porte et un soupir» (1963): a door hinge as soloist.

patterns.title: Montage of causes
patterns.principle: Collage of concrete debris — the source of the sound is hidden.
patterns.reference: Musique concrète: Schaeffer and Henry, Rue de l'Université studio.

patterns.title: El Cimarrón
patterns.principle: Dry storytelling voice and guitar gate — a fugitive slave's narrative.
patterns.reference: «El Cimarrón» (1970): recital for four performers, Montejo's story.

patterns.title: Political gesture
patterns.principle: Saturation and clicks — music as a position.
patterns.reference: Henze: a communist who moved to Italy; art as politics.

patterns.title: Night music
patterns.principle: Dynamic waves and soft layers — late Henze's lyricism.
patterns.reference: His late scores: a politician turned lyricist.

patterns.title: A Very Cellular Song
patterns.principle: Octave chant and a dry layer — a psychedelic folk hymn.
patterns.reference: Incredible String Band, «The Hangman's Beautiful Daughter» (1968).

patterns.title: Psychedelic folk
patterns.principle: Slow phase and modal resonances.
patterns.reference: ISB: folk passed through psychedelia and ethnicity.

patterns.title: Log Cabin Home in the Sky
patterns.principle: Choral cloud — polyphony of one voice.
patterns.reference: His multi-layered vocal arrangements in ISB.

patterns.title: Illiac Suite
patterns.principle: Stochastic permutation of fragments — the first computer score.
patterns.reference: «Illiac Suite» (1957), Hiller and Isaacson: ILLIAC I composes a string quartet.

patterns.title: Markov transitions
patterns.principle: Grains run sequentially but with probabilistic jumps.
patterns.reference: Markov chains — his method of generating musical text.

patterns.title: HPSCHD
patterns.principle: Seven clouds and clicks — computer anarchy with Cage.
patterns.reference: «HPSCHD» (1969), Hiller and Cage: 7 harpsichords, 51 tapes, a mainframe.

patterns.title: Henry Cow: angular riffs
patterns.principle: Collage of angular debris and a gate — rock as chamber avant-garde.
patterns.reference: Henry Cow (1968–78): rock in opposition, compositional complexity.

patterns.title: Polymeter 5 and 7
patterns.principle: Gate 5+7 against clicks — two meters at once.
patterns.reference: His scores: polymeter as political form.

patterns.title: Living in the Heart of the Beast
patterns.principle: Reverse tape and saturation — fury of form.
patterns.reference: «In Praise of Learning» (1975): a 15-minute composition by Hodgkinson.

patterns.title: Haramand Plane
patterns.principle: Irregular fast clicks and grains — ritual streaming.
patterns.reference: «Haramand Plane» (1970s): ritual performances with electronics.

patterns.title: Streaming
patterns.principle: Dense jitter-granulate at 40 grains per second — formless stream.
patterns.reference: His streaming — music as continuous ritual flow.

patterns.title: Breath of ritual
patterns.principle: Near silence and tremolo — the performer's body in the sound.
patterns.reference: Hunt: Texan shaman of electronics, video, and gesture.

patterns.title: Sapporo
patterns.principle: Long freeze and slow tremolo — sustained tones.
patterns.reference: «Sapporo» (1962): long tones with electronics.

patterns.title: Extended Voices
patterns.principle: Formant choir and harmonic layers — extended voice.
patterns.reference: «Extended Voices» (1967): voices and electronics.

patterns.title: Sustained tones
patterns.principle: Drone oscillator and a quiet dry layer — time as material.
patterns.reference: His music: silence, duration, one sound.

patterns.title: Two chapels
patterns.principle: Two layers in different tunings and tempos, hard-panned L/R — collision of marches.
patterns.reference: «Putnam's Camp» from «Three Places in New England»: two orchestras play different things at once.

patterns.title: The Unanswered Question
patterns.principle: Question-oscillator and cloud-answer — an eternal dialogue.
patterns.reference: «The Unanswered Question» (1908): trumpet asks, flutes do not answer.

patterns.title: Central Park in the Dark
patterns.principle: Nocturnal cloud and distant clicks — urban darkness.
patterns.reference: «Central Park in the Dark» (1906): night sounds of New York.

patterns.title: Match: duel
patterns.principle: Panoramic L/R duel and a gate — two cellists compete.
patterns.reference: «Match» (1964): two cellists and a percussionist-referee.

patterns.title: Absurdist montage
patterns.principle: Collage and clicks — theater of the absurd in sound.
patterns.reference: Kagel: instrumental theater, humor as method.

patterns.title: Gesture theater
patterns.principle: Formant replies and stutters — sound as stage action.
patterns.reference: His mute instruments are prescribed gestures, not notes.

patterns.title: Topology of time
patterns.principle: Continuous tempo deformation — time as a topological space.
patterns.reference: Kamin: structures from topology, prosody, and general systems theory.

patterns.title: Prosody
patterns.principle: Syllable-grains and speech gate — prosodic segmentation.
patterns.reference: His oneiric forms: fictional languages and conceptual mythologies.

patterns.title: Echo to a friend
patterns.principle: 660 Hz bell and long echo — a motif connected to block 015 Brody.
patterns.reference: Kamin and Brody died together on April 11, 2010.

patterns.title: Encounters
patterns.principle: Percussive clicks in space — a meeting of percussion.
patterns.reference: «Encounters» (1970s): Kraft's percussion theater.

patterns.title: Percussion theater
patterns.principle: Stream transients and panorama — attacks as characters.
patterns.reference: Kraft: percussionist of the Los Angeles Philharmonic, percussionist-composer.

patterns.title: Rhythm mass
patterns.principle: Dense gate and a cloud — rhythmic mass.
patterns.reference: His percussion ensembles: rhythm as architecture.

patterns.title: Fremdarbeit: outsourcing
patterns.principle: Demonstratively cheap processing: 5-bit and decimation — labor outsourced.
patterns.reference: «Fremdarbeit» (2009): composition commissioned from a Chinese composer and an Indian programmer.

patterns.title: Product placements
patterns.principle: 15 ms microsamples, 40 per second — tens of thousands of other people's sounds as a gesture.
patterns.reference: «product placements» (2008): 70,261 microsamples of other people's music.

patterns.title: Charts Music
patterns.principle: Oscillator pitch follows the stream's loudness — curve sonification.
patterns.reference: «Charts Music» (2009): stock charts sung through Auto-Tune.

patterns.title: Musique concrète instrumentale
patterns.principle: Tonal is suppressed, attacks, rustles, breath of the stream remain.
patterns.reference: «Pression» (1969): sound equals the way it is produced, bow noise matters more than the note.

patterns.title: Rustles
patterns.principle: High grains and a highpass — the noise matter of the instrument.
patterns.reference: His instrumental concrete music: the body of the instrument as source.

patterns.title: Gran Torso
patterns.principle: Transients and bow resonances — string quartet as noise theater.
patterns.reference: «Gran Torso» (1972): quartet No. 1, radical noise writing.

patterns.title: Revolution 9
patterns.principle: Collage of loops and reverse — sonic chaos as composition.
patterns.reference: «Revolution 9» (1968): eight minutes of tape loops, «number nine».

patterns.title: Number nine
patterns.principle: One loop repeats with panoramic drift — an obsessive phrase.
patterns.reference: The «number nine» voice from a Royal Schools of Music test record.

patterns.title: Tomorrow Never Knows
patterns.principle: Echo, phase, and resonances — the Revolver tape loops.
patterns.reference: «Tomorrow Never Knows» (1966): five tape loops spinning in the studio.

patterns.title: Micropolyphony
patterns.principle: 48 copies detuned ±15 cents — a dense shimmering cloud.
patterns.reference: «Atmosphères» (1961): 87 voices, not one distinguishable line.

patterns.title: Poème symphonique
patterns.principle: 24 metronomes in different tempos winding down one by one (out of 100 original).
patterns.reference: «Poème symphonique» (1962): 100 metronomes wound up and left to themselves.

patterns.title: Lux Aeterna
patterns.principle: 16 slow voices and resonances — the light of eternity.
patterns.reference: «Lux Aeterna» (1966): 16 voices, canon without rhythm.

patterns.title: World Rhythms
patterns.principle: Quiet dry layer and gong-clicks — rivers and a gong.
patterns.reference: «World Rhythms» (1975): 10-channel tape, gong and river sounds.

patterns.title: Danube
patterns.principle: Water filter and stream-grains — a sound map of a river.
patterns.reference: «A Sound Map of the Danube» (2005): 86 places along the river.

patterns.title: Sound geography
patterns.principle: Slow diffusion — the place sounds itself.
patterns.reference: Lockwood: listening as ecology, sound as place.

patterns.title: I Am Sitting in a Room
patterns.principle: Resonators on the stream's reference frequencies are excited one by one — the room amplifies itself.
patterns.reference: «I Am Sitting in a Room» (1969): room re-recorded over itself, resonances defeat speech.

patterns.title: Vespers
patterns.principle: Echolocation clicks and echo — sound feels its way through space.
patterns.reference: «Vespers» (1961): performers with sondols orient by echo like bats.

patterns.title: Music on a Long Thin Wire
patterns.principle: Drone and slow tremolo — the wire sings itself.
patterns.reference: «Music on a Long Thin Wire» (1977): an electromagnet excites a 20-meter wire.

patterns.title: Triola
patterns.principle: Tape speed fluctuates — GRM time jumps.
patterns.reference: «Triola» (1978): tape and orchestra, playing with time.

patterns.title: Zeitsprünge
patterns.principle: Granular morph with sharp tempo jumps.
patterns.reference: His music: montage of time, jumps between states.

patterns.title: Spectral theater
patterns.principle: Grains and formants — sound as a stage.
patterns.reference: Malec: Croatian-French master of musique concrète.

patterns.title: Nirvana Symphony
patterns.principle: Bon-shō bell resonances 1 : 2.4 : 4.1 : 6.8 — Buddhist tolling.
patterns.reference: «Nirvana Symphony» (1958): bon-shō bells as harmonic model.

patterns.title: Mandala
patterns.principle: Freeze and drone — a sound mandala.
patterns.reference: «Mandala Symphony» (1960): Buddhist cosmology in sound.

patterns.title: Bon-shō
patterns.principle: A bell with long decay and echo — the strike and its shadow.
patterns.reference: Bon-shō: a Japanese temple bell that sounds for minutes.

patterns.title: Mode 2: octatonic
patterns.principle: Resonators and harmonization on the octatonic grid — a mode of limited transposition.
patterns.reference: «Technique de mon langage musical» (1944): seven modes of limited transposition.

patterns.title: Non-retrogradable rhythms
patterns.principle: Palindromic gate 3-5-7-5-3 — a rhythm readable in both directions.
patterns.reference: His non-retrogradable rhythms: palindromes as a theological symbol.

patterns.title: Birds
patterns.principle: Chirp-grains and high transposition — a bird catalog.
patterns.reference: «Catalogue d'oiseaux» (1958): 13 pieces, 77 bird species.

patterns.title: Polytonality
patterns.principle: Two harmonic layers in a tritone relation — two keys at once.
patterns.reference: «Le Bœuf sur le toit» (1919), «Saudades do Brasil»: polytonality as a signature.

patterns.title: Saudades do Brasil
patterns.principle: Samba gate and harmonization — Brazilian memory.
patterns.reference: «Saudades do Brasil» (1920): 12 dances written after Brazil.

patterns.title: Tenderness
patterns.principle: Dry sound and soft layers — a lyricist inside Les Six.
patterns.reference: Milhaud: lyricism and polyphony of keys, La Six.

patterns.title: Marimba Spiritual
patterns.principle: Wooden resonances and an accelerating gate — a marimba ritual.
patterns.reference: «Marimba Spiritual» (1984): marimba and percussion, a prayer for repose.

patterns.title: Ritual ostinato
patterns.principle: Repeating gate and clicks — a growing ritual.
patterns.reference: His percussion pieces: ostinato as incantation.

patterns.title: Wood and skin
patterns.principle: Wooden resonances and transients — the instrument's material.
patterns.reference: Miki revived Japanese instruments in contemporary music.

patterns.title: Songmy
patterns.principle: Hard saturation and collage — political electronics.
patterns.reference: «Sing Me a Song of Songmy» (1971) with Freddie Hubbard: protest on tape.

patterns.title: Aggressive montage
patterns.principle: Sharp splices and speed jumps — tape as a weapon.
patterns.reference: His montage: violence of form as a political statement.

patterns.title: Political tape
patterns.principle: Ring modulation and echo — a voice distorted by the system.
patterns.reference: Mimaroglu: Turkish-American pioneer of electronic music.

patterns.title: Pithecanthropus Erectus
patterns.principle: Free canon and dynamic waves — collective improvisation.
patterns.reference: «Pithecanthropus Erectus» (1956): a suite of the rise and fall of man.

patterns.title: The Clown
patterns.principle: Swing gate and formant storytelling — jazz as theater.
patterns.reference: «The Clown» (1957): narrator and orchestra, tragicomedy.

patterns.title: Double bass growl
patterns.principle: Low resonances and tremolo — a growling bass.
patterns.reference: His bass: from tenderness to fury, always on the cutting edge.

patterns.title: Open tunings
patterns.principle: Resonators of the open C-G-C-G-E chord — guitar in her tuning.
patterns.reference: Mitchell used about 50 open tunings; «Big Yellow Taxi» is open E.

patterns.title: Blue: vocal layers
patterns.principle: Harmonic layers over the dry voice — her polyphony.
patterns.reference: «Blue» (1971): she overdubbed all the vocal parts herself.

patterns.title: Dulcimer
patterns.principle: String resonances and gate — Appalachian dulcimer.
patterns.reference: «All I Want» (Blue): a dulcimer bought in Arkansas.

patterns.title: Tempo canon 17:18:19
patterns.principle: Three granular voices in tempos 17:18:19 — pitch unchanged, only speed.
patterns.reference: Studies for player piano: tempo canons, impossible for hands.

patterns.title: e : π
patterns.principle: Two voices in the irrational ratio e/π ≈ 0.865 — a canon that never converges.
patterns.reference: Study No. 40: canon in the ratio e:π.

patterns.title: Player piano roll
patterns.principle: Perforated gate and clicks — a mechanical roll.
patterns.reference: Nancarrow punched rolls by hand in Mexico City, for decades.

patterns.title: …sofferte onde serene…
patterns.principle: Near silence and long echo — calm waves of memory.
patterns.reference: «…sofferte onde serene…» (1976): piano and tape, bells of Venice.

patterns.title: Silence of resistance
patterns.principle: Rare events in near silence — silence as politics.
patterns.reference: Nono: a communist, silence as a form of resistance.

patterns.title: La fabbrica illuminata
patterns.principle: Factory transients and filter — the illuminated factory.
patterns.reference: «La fabbrica illuminata» (1964): workers' voices and factory noise.

patterns.title: Microtones
patterns.principle: Quarter-tone layers and a formant melisma — the Andalusian root.
patterns.reference: Ohana: microtonality, Lorca, African rhythms.

patterns.title: Lorca
patterns.principle: Dark gate and resonances — lament for Lorca.
patterns.reference: «Llanto por Ignacio Sánchez Mejías» (1950) — his requiem for Lorca.

patterns.title: African roots
patterns.principle: Polyrhythmic clicks and gate.
patterns.reference: Ohana was born in Casablanca; Africa is his rhythmic homeland.

patterns.title: De Natura Sonorum
patterns.principle: Dialectic of dry and granular — the natural against the formed.
patterns.reference: «De Natura Sonorum» (1975): 12 studies on the nature of sound.

patterns.title: Violostries
patterns.principle: Dry instrument and a ring shadow — violin and tape.
patterns.reference: «Violostries» (1964): violin and tape in dialogue.

patterns.title: Matter / form
patterns.principle: Freeze morphs into granulation — matter takes form.
patterns.reference: GRM: sound as matter, montage as form.

patterns.title: 43 steps
patterns.principle: Harmonization in just ratios of his 43-step tuning.
patterns.reference: «Genesis of a Music» (1949): 43 tones per octave, own instruments.

patterns.title: Cloud chambers
patterns.principle: Glass resonances — his cloud chambers made of glass.
patterns.reference: Cloud-Chamber Bowls: glass jars tuned by him.

patterns.title: Bitter Music
patterns.principle: Dry voice and speech gate — music of speech.
patterns.reference: «Bitter Music» (1930s): a hobo's diary, speech as melody.

patterns.title: Threnody: 52 strings
patterns.principle: 52 micro-copies with diverging glissandi from the spectral center.
patterns.reference: «Threnody to the Victims of Hiroshima» (1960): 52 strings, clusters and extended techniques.

patterns.title: Cluster mass
patterns.principle: Wide semitone cluster and saturation — a sound mass.
patterns.reference: His sonorism of the 1960s: sound as mass, not line.

patterns.title: Polymorphia
patterns.principle: The cloud converges back — glissando toward the center.
patterns.reference: «Polymorphia» (1961): 48 strings, brain EEG became the score.

patterns.title: Come Out: phase shift
patterns.principle: A delayed copy of the stream runs ahead — 1% per second divergence.
patterns.reference: «Come Out» (1966): Harlem Six voice, two tapes drift out of phase.

patterns.title: It's Gonna Rain
patterns.principle: Faster phase drift and echo — process as music.
patterns.reference: «It's Gonna Rain» (1965): Brother Walter's sermon, phase canon.

patterns.title: Pendulum Music
patterns.principle: Feedback sweep and panorama — swinging microphones.
patterns.reference: «Pendulum Music» (1968): microphones swing over speakers, feedback whistle.

patterns.title: Sensemayá
patterns.principle: Ritual seven-beat ostinato gate and dark resonances — a snake incantation.
patterns.reference: «Sensemayá» (1938): a song to kill a snake, on a poem by Nicolás Guillén.

patterns.title: Snake chant
patterns.principle: Minor-second harmonization and tremolo — a hypnotic chant.
patterns.reference: His melodics: Mexican archaism and modernism.

patterns.title: Ritual acceleration
patterns.principle: Gate accelerates, clicks grow — ritual to frenzy.
patterns.reference: Revueltas: rhythm as collective trance.

patterns.title: The Angel of Death
patterns.principle: Morphing between domains and incidences — memory of a motif.
patterns.reference: «The Angel of Death» (2001): studied by IRCAM psychoacousticians and McAdams.

patterns.title: Whispers Out of Time
patterns.principle: Whisper-grains and echo — whispers outside time.
patterns.reference: «Whispers Out of Time» (1988), Pulitzer: strings and memory.

patterns.title: Memory of a motif
patterns.principle: Collage with returns — the motif is recognized through distortion.
patterns.reference: His studies of musical memory: recognition through transformations.

patterns.title: Rítmicas V/VI
patterns.principle: Stream transients and wooden clicks — pure percussion without pitch.
patterns.reference: «Rítmicas» V and VI (1930) — percussion only, earlier than Varèse's «Ionisation».

patterns.title: Afro-Cuban clave
patterns.principle: Clave gate 3-2 — the key to Afro-Cuban rhythm.
patterns.reference: Roldán: Afro-Cuban rhythms in Cuban academic music.

patterns.title: Percussion without pitch
patterns.principle: Wooden and metallic resonances with gate.
patterns.reference: His percussion ensembles: rhythm and timbre instead of melody.

patterns.title: Coming Together
patterns.principle: Additive accumulation of fragments: a, a+b, a+b+c… — the process of freedom.
patterns.reference: «Coming Together» (1971): an Attica prisoner's text, additive process.

patterns.title: The People United
patterns.principle: Loop-variations: the motif repeats with changes — 36 variations in miniature.
patterns.reference: «The People United Will Never Be Defeated!» (1975): 36 variations.

patterns.title: Attica
patterns.principle: Dry voice and gate — speech as music.
patterns.reference: «Attica» (1972): political speech, sung and spoken.

patterns.title: Vexations: 840 repeats
patterns.principle: 840 micro-repeats of a motif in 10 s = 84 Hz: repetition becomes pitch.
patterns.reference: «Vexations» (1893): instruction to repeat 840 times. Greetings to Stockhausen's «…wie die Zeit vergeht…».

patterns.title: Musique d'ameublement
patterns.principle: Quiet dry sound in a room echo — furniture music.
patterns.reference: «Musique d'ameublement» (1917): music not listened to.

patterns.title: Relâche
patterns.principle: Absurd loop and clicks — the entr'acte as a joke.
patterns.reference: «Relâche» (1924): a ballet with an entr'acte, cinema, and satire.

patterns.title: One note
patterns.principle: Resonator on the stream's reference frequency and ±2 cent beats — one note from inside.
patterns.reference: «Quattro pezzi su una nota sola» (1959): four pieces on one note.

patterns.title: Inside the overtones
patterns.principle: Resonators on overtones 1..5 slowly open.
patterns.reference: His method: sound as a living organism with an inner life.

patterns.title: Unfolding
patterns.principle: Freeze and a dynamic wave — sound breathes.
patterns.reference: Scelsi: sound is not a point but a sphere.

patterns.title: 12-tone row
patterns.principle: Resonators on the 12-tone grid and row permutation of fragments.
patterns.reference: The 12-tone method (1923): composition with 12 tones related only to each other.

patterns.title: Sprechstimme
patterns.principle: Sliding formant and grains — speech between singing and speaking.
patterns.reference: «Pierrot lunaire» (1912): Sprechstimme marked with crosses on the notes.

patterns.title: Emancipation of dissonance
patterns.principle: Dissonant cloud and harmonization — dissonance without resolution.
patterns.reference: Emancipation of dissonance: dissonance no longer requires resolution.

patterns.title: In futurum: score of rests
patterns.principle: Near silence: the stream is muted down to the noise floor — sound that is almost not.
patterns.reference: «In futurum» (1919): the entire score is rests, 33 years before Cage's 4′33″.

patterns.title: Jazz-dance
patterns.principle: Swing gate and harmonization — 1920s jazz in academic fabric.
patterns.reference: His «5 Etudes de Jazz» (1926) and jazz movements of suites.

patterns.title: Dada collage
patterns.principle: Collage and clicks — a Dadaist gesture.
patterns.reference: Schulhoff: Dadaist, friend of Hausmann, died in the Wülzburg concentration camp.

patterns.title: Mystic chord
patterns.principle: Resonators C–F#–B♭–E–A–D — his six-note sonority.
patterns.reference: «Prometheus» (1910): the mystic chord as harmonic foundation.

patterns.title: Light-music
patterns.principle: Spectral tilt slowly brightens — color as harmony.
patterns.reference: Clavier à lumières: he saw the colors of keys.

patterns.title: Vers la flamme
patterns.principle: Dynamic wave and cloud — toward the flame.
patterns.reference: «Vers la flamme» (1914): growth from darkness to blinding light.

patterns.title: Apocalypse
patterns.principle: Formant opera and granulation — electronic voice theater.
patterns.reference: «Apocalypse» (1990s): Shields's electronic opera.

patterns.title: Shaman
patterns.principle: Ritual resonances and tremolo — a shamanic voice.
patterns.reference: Her «Shaman»: ritual and electronics.

patterns.title: Columbia-Princeton
patterns.principle: Ring modulation and tape montage — her school.
patterns.reference: Shields studied with Ussachevsky at the Columbia-Princeton Electronic Music Center.

patterns.title: Robot saxophone
patterns.principle: Mechanical stutter and saxophone formant — a robot plays a solo.
patterns.reference: Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band: his robot saxophonist on stage.

patterns.title: Trouser Press
patterns.principle: Mechanical gate and saturation — a trouser press as an instrument.
patterns.reference: His trouser press — an absurd mechanical performance.

patterns.title: Vaudeville
patterns.principle: Panorama and absurd clicks — English vaudeville.
patterns.reference: Bonzo Dog Band: Dada, vaudeville, and rock.

patterns.title: Sir Henry at Rawlinson End
patterns.principle: Formant characters and dry narration — radio drama.
patterns.reference: «Sir Henry at Rawlinson End» (1970s): a surrealist saga.

patterns.title: Radio drama
patterns.principle: Collage and echo — radio play montage.
patterns.reference: His radio shows: voice as theater of the absurd.

patterns.title: Eccentricity
patterns.principle: Bells and gate — English eccentricity.
patterns.reference: Stanshall: voice of the Bonzo Dog Band, poet and eccentric.

patterns.title: Nurse With Wound
patterns.principle: Surrealist collage and echo — a waking dream.
patterns.reference: «Homotopy to Marie» (1982): a surrealist drone collage.

patterns.title: Drone collage
patterns.principle: Dark cloud and freeze — drone as a dream.
patterns.reference: Nurse With Wound: surrealism in sound, collage as method.

patterns.title: Vinyl ghost
patterns.principle: Crushed tape and crackle-clicks — a ghost of vinyl.
patterns.reference: His collages: vinyl crackle as a texture of memory.

patterns.title: Mixtur: ring modulation
patterns.principle: Ring-mod of the live stream with its own carrier — sum and difference frequencies.
patterns.reference: «Mixtur» (1964): orchestra, four ring modulators, sine tones.

patterns.title: Kontakte: rotation
patterns.principle: Ring modulation and spatial rotation — sound flies in a circle.
patterns.reference: «Kontakte» (1959–60): electronics, piano, percussion; rotation in four channels.

patterns.title: Mantra: two pianos
patterns.principle: Two ring layers and resonances — a mantra of 13 sounds.
patterns.reference: «Mantra» (1970): two pianos with ring modulation, 13-sound formula.

patterns.title: Space Echo
patterns.principle: Tape echo with wow and flutter and a spring resonance — cosmos.
patterns.reference: His Arkestra: tape echo, spring reverb, detuned keyboards.

patterns.title: Cosmic tuning
patterns.principle: Detuned cloud and oscillator — keyboards gone into space.
patterns.reference: Sun Ra: «Space is the Place», detuned clavioline and solovox.

patterns.title: Call of the horns
patterns.principle: Brass resonances in space — a call from afar.
patterns.reference: His Arkestra: horns as signals between worlds.

patterns.title: Ma: the space between
patterns.principle: Rare resonant events in silence — ma, emptiness as form.
patterns.reference: His aesthetic of ma: the silence between sounds matters more than the sounds.

patterns.title: Sky, Horse and Death
patterns.principle: Concrete collage — sky, horse, death on tape.
patterns.reference: «Sky, Horse and Death» (1958): his first concrete piece.

patterns.title: Garden
patterns.principle: Garden echo and a quiet dry layer — sound as a garden.
patterns.reference: Takemitsu: garden as compositional model, «Water Ways».

patterns.title: D.I.Y. circuit bending
patterns.principle: Crushed tape and stutters — home-made electronics.
patterns.reference: Baltimore conceptualist: lo-fi, d.i.y., absurdity as method.

patterns.title: Self-interruption
patterns.principle: Collage interrupted by silence — the work argues with itself.
patterns.reference: His performances: intentional glitches and self-destruction of form.

patterns.title: Low fidelity
patterns.principle: Cassette crush and echo — fidelity of low precision.
patterns.reference: Lo-fi as an aesthetic position, not a deficiency.

patterns.title: Poème électronique
patterns.principle: Spatial sweeps and siren glissando — the Philips Pavilion.
patterns.reference: «Poème électronique» (1958): 425 loudspeakers of the Philips Pavilion, Brussels.

patterns.title: Déserts: blocks
patterns.principle: Alternation of dry instrumental and electronic blocks.
patterns.reference: «Déserts» (1954): instrumental blocks and tape interpolations.

patterns.title: Sirens
patterns.principle: Siren glissandi and saturation — organized sound.
patterns.reference: «Ionisation» (1931) and «Amériques»: sirens as instruments.

patterns.title: Modal folk
patterns.principle: Dorian resonances and drone harmonization — the Celtic root.
patterns.reference: Incredible String Band: Celtic folk, ethnicity, and psychedelia.

patterns.title: Multi-instrumental
patterns.principle: Different resonator banks with gate — one person, many instruments.
patterns.reference: Williamson: harp, guitar, flute, jaw harp — all himself.

patterns.title: Drone tanpura
patterns.principle: Drone oscillator and dry layer — the Indian root of ISB.
patterns.reference: ISB brought tanpura and raga into psychedelic folk.

patterns.title: Sometimes
patterns.principle: Spiritual resonances and ring modulation — voice and tape.
patterns.reference: «Sometimes» (1976): tenor and tape, transformation of the spiritual «Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child».

patterns.title: Heterogeneous sound principle
patterns.principle: Grains, clicks, and resonances at once — the heterogeneous sound ideal.
patterns.reference: His term (1983): African-American music as heterogeneity of timbres.

patterns.title: Call-response
patterns.principle: Dry call and echo-answer — antiphony.
patterns.reference: Call-and-response: structure of African-American musical speech.

patterns.title: Red Bird: voice → bird
patterns.principle: Granular morph from speech grains to bird ones — sonic metamorphosis.
patterns.reference: «Red Bird» (1977): voice, birds, machines — a political allegory of transformations.

patterns.title: Audible Design: taxonomy
patterns.principle: Dry → freeze → granulation: three transformations from his book.
patterns.reference: «Audible Design» (1994) — a theory of sonic transformations, the methodological basis of this project.

patterns.title: CDP spectrum
patterns.principle: Freeze morphs into a resonator spectrum — his Composers Desktop Project.
patterns.reference: Wishart co-founded CDP (1986): spectral tools for everyone.

patterns.title: Duo for Pianists: cues
patterns.principle: Gate reacts to the previous event — a cybernetic score.
patterns.reference: «Duo for Pianists» (1957): the performer chooses by cue signals.

patterns.title: Burdocks
patterns.principle: Free cloud and clicks — an anarchic ensemble.
patterns.reference: «Burdocks» (1971): for any number of performers, anarchist form.

patterns.title: Agreement
patterns.principle: Free canon and a dry layer — coordination without a conductor.
patterns.reference: Wolff: music as social agreement among free people.

patterns.title: Montage of contrasts
patterns.principle: Sharp splices of opposing characters — dialectical montage.
patterns.reference: Wolpe: montage of contrasts, Brecht and Eisler in New York.

patterns.title: Battle Piece
patterns.principle: Saturation and gate — a piano battle.
patterns.reference: «Battle Piece» (1943–47): fury of form, a political gesture.

patterns.title: Form IV: broken sequences
patterns.principle: Grains tear the sequence apart — broken sequences.
patterns.reference: «Form IV: Broken Sequences» (1978): late, free form.

patterns.title: Time's Encomium
patterns.principle: Serial oscillator and ring modulation — the RCA Mark II.
patterns.reference: «Time's Encomium» (1969), Pulitzer: the RCA Mark II synthesizer, time as material.

patterns.title: Fractal slicing
patterns.principle: Self-similar splice: fragments of fragments — fractal form.
patterns.reference: Wuorinen: fractals and self-similarity in musical structure.

patterns.title: 12-tone grid + phase
patterns.principle: 12-tone grid resonators and phase drift.
patterns.reference: His serialism: 12 tones, strict organization of time.
